security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, defensive security guidance, or documented Higgsfield workflow references rather than active malicious code. One critical issue is confirmed: SKILL.md instructs agents to run a remote installer through the shell, which is unsafe without pinning, verification, and explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the command with a pinned release, checksum or signature verification, and explicit user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires broad local shell and deployment actions.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact commands that may run and require confirmation before installs, deletes, secret changes, and production deploys.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples contain many dangerous pattern names and external URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as non-executable guidance and keep risky strings inside clearly marked security reference sections.

content.value_statement: Launching a polished web product requires setup, design, security, and deployment steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Higgsfield CLI website and app workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates new website or app projects with the required Higgsfield CLI type choice.
Guides React 19 and TanStack Start implementation inside the generated app workspace.
Applies separate design guidance for standalone websites and Higgsfield-integrated apps.
Supports auth, fnf SDK, D1, R2, KV, Durable Object, and container guidance for app builds.
Defines preview, publish, SEO, cover image, and security review workflows.
Explains when to ask the user before production deploys or interactive authentication.
limitations: Requires the Higgsfield CLI, git, bun, and local shell access.
Can deploy only after the user has authenticated with Higgsfield.
Does not generate standalone media assets outside a website or app project.
Remote CLI installation should require explicit user review because it runs shell code.

use_cases.title: Launch a marketing site
use_cases.description: Create a standalone branded website with custom visuals, SEO metadata, preview deploys, and publish checks.

use_cases.title: Build a generation app
use_cases.description: Create a Higgsfield-integrated app with sign-in, generation workflows, Quanta UI guidance, and fnf SDK patterns.

use_cases.title: Polish an existing project
use_cases.description: Improve layout, security, auth, metadata, cover assets, and deployment readiness for an existing Higgsfield project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic website
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a preview website for my new product. Use the standalone website flow and ask me if any required choice is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Design a branded landing page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a branded landing page with strong visual direction, responsive sections, SEO metadata, and a preview deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Build an AI generation app
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Higgsfield app where signed-in users can generate media, review results, and see generation history.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for production release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Higgsfield app for auth, storage, SEO, cover image, and security issues, then deploy preview and prepare production publish steps.

output_examples.input: Build a landing page for a design agency.
output_examples.output: A preview-ready Higgsfield website with custom brand direction, responsive sections, SEO metadata, and clear publish blockers if any remain.

output_examples.input: Create an image generation app for signed-in users.
output_examples.output: An app plan and implementation path with Higgsfield sign-in, fnf SDK usage, generation controls, history views, and preview deployment.
A concise release review covering auth, storage, security, SEO, cover image quality, deployment status, and remaining production steps.

best_practices: Confirm website versus app before creating any project.
Keep preview deploys as the default and ask before production publish.
Review security, SEO, auth, and storage guidance before handling user data.
anti_patterns: Installing or deploying through the CLI without explicit user consent.
Using the standalone website flow for AI media generation products.
Exposing tokens, raw IDs, or infrastructure details in user-facing messages.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It builds Higgsfield websites and Higgsfield-integrated web apps using the Higgsfield CLI and React-based project structure.

faq.question: When should I choose website versus app?
faq.answer: Choose website for standalone marketing or product sites. Choose app when the product uses Higgsfield sign-in, generation, credits, or history.

faq.question: Does it require shell access?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses Bash, the Higgsfield CLI, git, bun, local files, and deploy commands.

faq.question: Can it deploy to production?
faq.answer: Yes, but production deployment should happen only after the user explicitly asks to publish or go live.

faq.question: Does it support AI generation apps?
faq.answer: Yes. Generation products use the app flow with Higgsfield sign-in, fnf SDK guidance, and account-based generation credits.

faq.question: Is remote CLI installation safe?
faq.answer: It should be reviewed first. The current skill includes a remote install command, which security audits should treat as high risk.
